questions.question: Which sign means your vehicle's brakes need repair?

options.text: The brake pads are not covered in grease.
The brake pads are not covered in oil.
The brake pads are worn thin.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake pads are worn thin.
questions.explanation: Check your brakes for these problems: cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, shoes that are broken or missing, and shoes worn too thin.

questions.question: How much compressed air do air tanks usually hold?

options.text: Enough for one stop before needing to refill.
Enough for several stops before needing to refill.
Enough for a day's worth of braking.
Enough for unlimited stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Enough for several stops before needing to refill.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in an air brake system hold enough compressed air for the brakes to work several times before needing to refill.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most heavy-duty vehicles use?

options.text: Air brakes
Solid brakes
Liquid brakes
Gravity brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Air brakes
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems for safety.

questions.question: How many mirrors should a registered vehicle have?

options.text: A mirror on the left side only.
Mirrors on both the left and right sides.
A mirror on the right side only.
Only a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mirrors on both the left and right sides.
questions.explanation: Vehicles need mirrors on both sides so you can see all around your vehicle. Check your mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: Which surface gives you the least traction?

options.text: Dry ice
Wet ice
Wet pavement
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving on melting ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: While driving, what should you do with your mirrors?

options.text: Do not use them.
Use them only when changing lanes.
Check them regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic around you and spot any problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Cracked drums
Shoes with oil or grease on them
Shoes worn thin
Pads free of oil or grease

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads free of oil or grease
questions.explanation: Check your brakes for these problems: cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, shoes that are broken or missing, and shoes worn too thin.

questions.question: How should you complete a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Change the order each time.
Complete it in the same order every time.
Only do it when the weather is sunny.
Skip it if you think the vehicle is in good condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete it in the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Use the same order for every pre-trip inspection. This helps you learn the steps and makes sure you check everything.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you do with engine belts?

options.text: Loosen them.
Check them for tightness.
Inspect them only if they look frayed.
Do not inspect them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them for tightness.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check engine belts for tightness and wear.

questions.question: What does the emergency brake system use?

options.text: Only parts from the parking brake system.
Only parts from the service brake system.
Parts from both the parking and service brake systems.
Only parts unique to the emergency brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts from both the parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three braking systems: a service brake system, a parking brake system, and an emergency brake system. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What should you do if you suspect a leak in radioactive material cargo?

options.text: Go to the local fire department.
Pick up any loose pieces of radioactive material.
Keep driving as long as you do not touch the affected areas.
Stop driving the vehicle until it has been cleaned.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop driving the vehicle until it has been cleaned.
questions.explanation: If you suspect a leak or broken package in radioactive material, tell your dispatcher or supervisor right away. Do not touch or breathe in the material. Do not drive the vehicle until it has been cleaned or checked with a survey meter.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal, then the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash the brake lights.
Swerve side to side to get attention.
Turn all lights on and off several times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash the brake lights.
questions.explanation: Tap your brake pedal lightly a few times to make the brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: Emergency equipment like a fire extinguisher is:

options.text: Only needed for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Only needed for interstate travel.
Required on all commercial vehicles.
Only required when carrying passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required on all commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged and rated fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:

options.text: It recently rained.
The nuts are loose.
The tires need to be replaced.
The nuts are too tight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts usually means they are loose. Check how tight the nuts are if you see rust in that area.

questions.question: A package with liquid containers must display:

options.text: Arrows showing which way is up.
A return address.
The number of containers inside.
The word "fragile."

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows showing which way is up.
questions.explanation: Packages containing liquids must display arrows pointing the correct upright direction. These packages must be placed facing the correct way.

questions.question: After a crash, basic procedures should include all of the following except:

options.text: Protecting the area.
Notifying authorities.
Caring for the injured.
Driving away without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving away without stopping.
questions.explanation: After a crash, you must protect the area, notify authorities, and care for anyone injured. It is important to protect the accident site right away to prevent another crash in the same location.

questions.question: Which sign does not mean a person is drowsy?

options.text: Frequent blinking
Drifting from your lane
Feeling hungry
Yawning

questions.correctAnswerText: Feeling hungry
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is dangerous and must be avoided. Signs of drowsiness include frequent blinking, eyes closing or going out of focus on their own, yawning, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: The application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the braking system.
The air pressure coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: When driving into fog, you should:

options.text: Use high beam headlights.
Speed up.
Turn up the radio volume.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: It is best to avoid driving in fog. If you must drive through fog, slow down before you reach it.

questions.question: You should not use the parking brake when:

options.text: Your vehicle is on level ground.
Your vehicle is on a slight slope.
Your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
Your other braking systems are working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if the brakes are very hot from going down a steep hill or if the brakes are wet in freezing temperatures. Using the parking brake when brakes are hot can damage them. Using brakes when wet in freezing weather can cause them to ice up and lock the vehicle.
